rules_audit.scope: Independent read-only audit of both supplied DOCX package contents and raw workbook calculations. Source files unchanged.

documents.package_scan: All 13 XML/relationship parts inspected; no comments, textboxes, headers/footers, tracked inserts/deletions, drawings or embedded files.
documents.locators: Paragraph numbers count all w:p elements in word/document.xml, including table cells.

relevant_paragraphs.6: Overview says projects may overlap either through physical closeness or scheduling around the same time.
relevant_paragraphs.60: Geographic threshold is within 25 mi; next sentence says closer than 25 mi.
relevant_paragraphs.62: Timeline overlap means the same build window.
relevant_paragraphs.63: Geographic overlap is primary; timeline is a strong secondary signal used together with it.

documents.package_scan: All 13 XML/relationship parts inspected; no comments, textboxes, headers/footers, tracked inserts/deletions, drawings or embedded files.

relevant_paragraphs.46: Use center-to-center distance; center is midpoint of two named sub-points, or the one located point. Straight-line/haversine acceptable. Pairs under 25 miles become overlap rows. Record in-service-date gap in days, as a lighter consideration.

documents.numeric_caution: The code example also contains timeout:25; this is an Overpass timeout, not another geographic threshold.

rule_findings.verdict: Consistent numeric threshold: 25 miles. No alternative mileage value found in body text or any other DOCX XML layer.
Ambiguous at exactly 25.0 miles: within can be read inclusively, but closer than and under imply strict less-than. No explicit <= operator is supplied.
rule_findings.recommended_documented_assumption: Use distance_mi < 25, consistent with the guide and explicit closer-than wording. Evaluate unrounded distance; disclose boundary convention.

rule_findings.verdict: Opening prose permits either closeness OR similar timing. Detailed prose and companion guide instead make geography the primary inclusion signal and timing secondary.
rule_findings.recommended_documented_assumption: Use geographic candidates for the main overlap table, display timing separately, and flag organizer clarification for whether distant timeline-only pairs should be a distinct class.

rule_findings.verdict: Challenge calls it strong secondary; guide calls it a lighter look. Neither specifies a day cutoff, score formula, numeric weight, or acceptable construction-window gap.
rule_findings.recommended_documented_assumption: Report date gap and precision visibly. Treat any scoring weights or time bands as team choices, not official rules.

rule_findings.verdict: No source conflict. Guide explicitly requests midpoint/single-point center distance. Neither source requires minimum route-to-route distance.
rule_findings.recommended_documented_assumption: Keep center distance as the rule metric; any closest-corridor distance is an additional metric and requires validated route geometry.

rule_findings.verdict: The guide asks for in-service-date gap, but the challenge describes same build window. An in-service date is a milestone, not a construction interval.
rule_findings.recommended_documented_assumption: A small milestone gap alone does not prove simultaneous construction; unknown start/end dates must remain unknown.

workbook.method: Arithmetic mean of the supplied endpoint latitudes and longitudes, falling back to the one supplied point; haversine with Earth radius 3958.7613 miles; absolute calendar-day difference of explicitly parsed US month/day/year dates.
workbook.formula_cache_check: All 10 center caches match independently calculated centers.
workbook.root_recomputed_json_match: All six distances match exactly and all six day gaps match.
limits: Distance and day-gap result cells are hardcoded, not formulas. Their current values reconcile, but do not auto-update from changes to coordinates or dates.
Dates mix text strings and Excel date values; parsing was explicit.
Arithmetic accuracy does not validate endpoint identity, project scope, date precision, current status or actual construction overlap.
Workbook examples do not settle the exact 25-mile boundary or numerical timeline weighting.

projects.geometry_verdict: A midpoint is only a coarse search anchor for a 35-mile line; use route geometry to test proximity anywhere along its length. The named endpoints are more consistent with scope than the partial-line samples, but still do not establish the route.
projects.irp_change_notes: IRP says advanced within 2025 versus prior ten-year plan and delayed from 2024 to 2025 versus prior IRP.
projects.later_search_result: No newer matching public schedule or actual completion confirmation located. Past planned date does not establish completed status.
projects.demo_disposition: Useful line-versus-midpoint control; no existing cross-utility overlap listed in workbook.

projects.name: JESUP - LUDOWICI PRIMARY 115KV REBUILD
projects.public_scope: Rebuild approximately 7.5 miles of the Jesup–North Jesup–Rayonier section of the broader Jesup–Ludowici Primary line.
projects.geometry_verdict: The full Jesup–Ludowici midpoint does not describe the narrower rebuilt section. Preserve North Jesup and Rayonier as segment identifiers pending public route evidence.
projects.later_search_result: No later matching official public schedule or completion record located. Current Jesup–Offerman work is a different named project and was not treated as this sample.
projects.ocr_check: A search-engine OCR lead suggested May 1, 2025 in a public exhibit mirror. Visual inspection of exhibit PDF page 17 shows June 1, 2025 instead, consistent with the supplied IRP. No schedule contradiction established.
projects.demo_disposition: Useful partial-line normalization example; no existing cross-utility overlap listed in workbook.

cross_utility_demo.recommended_claim: Public-source review can identify nearby projects, update stale dates, distinguish station equipment from line sections, and surface candidates for planner review.
cross_utility_demo.not_yet_supported: No verified GPC–DESC pair in these five samples has a proven shared construction footprint and simultaneous construction window from the sources reviewed.
cross_utility_demo.sample_candidate: DESC_3 / GPC_3 after the integrated Dominion and Georgia review. Latest milestones are 2026-12-01 and year-only 2028; the original 517-day gap is superseded for current-plan screening. Construction overlap remains unknown.

public_corridor_example.description: The 2026 order documents DESC's plan to combine work within the Okatie–McIntosh/Jasper corridor, reuse access and matting, and reconductor nearby lines. It separately says Jasper–Okatie #2 was being constructed.
public_corridor_example.distinction: The future reconductoring package is not the same schedule as initial Jasper–Okatie #2 construction. The Southern Company/Santee Cooper coordinated new-line proposal was an alternative considered, not the selected project.

cross_utility_demo.thurmond_disposition: Keep as an example showing that nearby planned assets can have widely separated dates. Do not portray the original 2024-versus-2033 pair as a confirmed current coordination opportunity.
cross_utility_demo.geometry_priority: For each project, retain component type, named work endpoints, source date, geometry provenance, and confidence. Do not calculate line-overlap certainty from center-to-center distances.

public_information_boundary.used: Supplied PUBLIC DISCLOSURE IRP, public Non-CEII SERTP reports and presentations, public regulatory order, and public OSM station labels independently checked in this integrated review.
public_information_boundary.not_used: Secure SERTP models, access-controlled CEII data, redacted supporting statements/costs, or inferred reconstruction of redactions.
public_information_boundary.label_caution: Some released documents retain generic CEII/confidential boilerplate or text-layer headings despite their PUBLIC DISCLOSURE/Non-CEII publication context. Only clearly released visible descriptions and dates were used. The public source label is not permission to obtain or infer restricted underlying models.

verification.status_limit: Latest confirmed plan means the newest matching source found in this bounded public review, not a guarantee of current construction status. None of the five samples has an actual completion date established here.

map_provenance.limits: Coordinates are OSM bounding-box centers, not surveyed centroids or utility-certified equipment coordinates. Element timestamps are map-edit dates, not construction status dates. User IDs and usernames omitted.
map_provenance.other_sample_query_method: Union of power=substation nwr features within 1200 meters of eight non-Savannah workbook points; out center meta. Reviewed features retained per project.

official_route_map.review: Visually inspected selected Jasper-to-Okatie corridor against roads and station areas. Image map does not supply a surveyed/georeferenced route. Study corridor width is not actual shared ROW or a cost quantity.

limits: Only these ten supplied examples were audited; public research was bounded and is not an exhaustive project inventory.
No reviewed pair establishes simultaneous construction, shared ROW or quantified savings.
Passed planned/need dates do not prove completion.
Guide-prescribed center distance is a screening proxy; route distance would require separately validated geometry.
Public disclosures and Non-CEII sources only; no secure models or redaction reconstruction.

source_preservation.note: Downloaded review files identified for provenance; source URLs are recorded in utility_research. These review caches are not distributed with the sample.
